== Biography ==
=== Merchant family and corrected index review — 31 October 2026 ===
The 1935 printed Glasgow burgess register has been visually inspected. On 14 September 1795 John Glasgow, merchant, entered as husband of Helen, lawful daughter of James Smith, mason and burgess/guild brother (printed p.197, PDF 207). On 1 July 1817 Alexander Glasgow, merchant in Wilson’s Court, Argyle Street, entered as eldest son of John Glasgow, merchant and burgess/guild brother (p.306, PDF 316). On 3 May 1844 John Glasgow, merchant, entered as a younger son of John Glasgow, merchant and burgess/guild brother (p.450, PDF 460). The first entry strongly identifies the maintained John-1348/Helen Smith household; the sons are supported comparisons with Alexander-971 and John-1355. The sons’ entries do not name their mother, and the three admissions must not be treated as a literal statement that all three men form one family. These are inspected published register transcriptions; the underlying manuscript admission registers are unread.

Burke’s Visitation, vol.2, printed armorial section p.67 (PDF 341), has now been read in the scan. It explicitly describes Alexander of Old Court, formerly Auchinraith, as eldest son of the late John Glasgow and Helen, daughter of James Smith, and grandson of Alexander Glasgow, merchant, and Agnes Monro of Edinburgh. The family passage was already quoted in the held biography; inspecting it is not discovery of a previously unknown grandfather name. The underlying Lyon matriculation remains unread.

The FamilySearch citation X17D-67M was checked directly: John was born 13 October 1771 and christened 19 October 1771 at Barony, parents Alexander Glasgow and Mary Munro. The copied 3 December 1765 date attached to that same citation is wrong; no independent 1765 record was verified in this review. This corrects the source account, not the vital fields or later identity of either modern John profile.

The independently identified John–Helen Smith merchant household now has inspected burgess evidence, and Burke explicitly gives its Alexander grandfather with a Monro wife associated with Edinburgh. That rare paired family description is more specific than the earlier chronological comparison with Alexander-1309’s Alexander/Mary Munro household, whose 1757 marriage was recorded in Edinburgh and Barony. The corrected 1771 Barony child fits the merchant’s possible generation. This modestly strengthens the whole existing father-profile hypothesis from 38% to 45% Possible; it does not make it Probable. Burke names Agnes Monro, not the documented Mary Munro of Alexander-1309’s couple. Their identity cannot be assumed, and the 1771 child has no inspected occupation, wife or estate bridge identifying him as the merchant rather than the Colinton account John-1304. The merchant’s circa 1770 birth is an inherited estimate, not independent corroboration. Retain both modern Johns and the current father selection, all mothers, vital fields and upstream grades. No new father attachment or merge follows. The 1741 childhood identification of Alexander-1309 is not certified by this review. Exact percentages are subjective judgements, not measured probabilities.<ref>[https://www.electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso51scotuoft.pdf Glasgow Burgesses and Guild Brethren 1751–1846 (1935)], pp.197,306,450 (PDF 207,316,460); [https://archive.org/details/visitationofseat185402burk/page/n340/mode/1up Burke, Visitation, vol.2, armorial p.67 (PDF 341)]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X17D-67M FamilySearch X17D-67M], inspected 31 October 2026. His father's name was John Glasgow, and his mother was Margaret Muckle. The baptismal records are part of the Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms collection, specifically from the year range 1738-1819. The archive reference for these records is OPR 677/2, and the entry is found on page 253.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-1309]] is assessed at 78% (probable). The retained John account names Alexander Glasgow and Mary Munro, matching the existing 1757-married couple and their recorded Glasgow child family. The cited X17 D-67 M event is 1765 while the account also gives 1771 and later adult material, so the exact child-to-adult identification is unsettled.

Complete father placement 78%; the 1765/1771 John events and John-1348 account are retained separately. No birth date or identity merge is selected.

Next useful test: Reconcile the two John event references and the Margaret Muckle adult household.

Source basis already held: [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X17D-67M https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X17D-67M]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.

=== Cached 1808–1814 family-event comparison, 24 October 2026 ===

Four saved Findmypast derivative transcripts for Kirknewton & East Calder record John Glasgow children born 2 December 1808, 25 January 1811 (two records with differing page/residence metadata), and 14 January 1814. They name a father John Glasgow and a mother rendered Mt/Margt Meikle. This is compatible with the existing Kirknewton household associated with Glasgow-1304 and Muckle-67, but the transcripts do not identify either adult profile. The existing adult family assessment and all vital fields are unchanged. Companion George indexes are held as one possible event, not independent confirmation. Original registers remain uninspected.

=== Colinton–Kirknewton working connection — 31 October 2026 ===

Alexander Glasgow-2695, the Midlothian agricultural labourer/ploughman, reports Colinton (also rendered Callington) as his birthplace, with census-implied births about 1801–1803. Alexander Glasgow-2718 was born 17 March 1799 and baptised 31 March at Colinton, residence Greysmill, explicitly to John Glasgow and Margaret Muckle. The distinctive birth parish, compatible two-to-four-year census age discrepancy and the family’s later Kirknewton context support identifying the childhood and adult accounts. John/Margaret’s recorded children at Kirknewton and East Calder in 1808–1814 provide a positive locality bridge to adult Alexander’s son John, born at Kirknewton about 1829. The first held son’s name John is only a minor, correlated clue. A bounded FamilySearch search for Alexander Glasgow, Colinton, 1795–1806 in Scotland Births and Baptisms returned the 1799child and two occurrences of the adult as a father; no closer childhood candidate was returned. This supports selecting the record-defined John Glasgow-1304 as the adult’s father at 65% subjective confidence, a new working attachment rather than a profile merger. <ref name="Colinton1799">[ https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4191802&tab=this Findmypast, Scotland Parish Births and Baptisms], Alexander Glasgow, birth17March1799/baptism31March1799, Greysmill, Colinton, John Glasgow and Margaret Muckle, OPR677/2 item3 p.253. Held provider transcript inspected22October2026; original register uninspected.</ref>

No inspected adult record explicitly names his parents; childhood-to-adult identity is inferred. The two-to-four-year age difference remains, and the bounded selected-localities birth index is incomplete: an unindexed Colinton child or a different adult identity for the 1799child could overturn the link. The census facts are held profile/index accounts, not newly read original images. The1799provider transcript was inspected earlier, original register uninspected. The Kirknewton Meikle entries are compatible family context, not independent proof of the adult identity. John-1304 represents the named Muckle father; his internally conflicting 1765/1771/c1790 childhood estimates and 78% upstream father assessment remain unresolved and unchanged. No mother attachment, exact birth replacement, wife identity resolution, or merger of 2695 and 2718 is proposed. The 1827blacksmith’s age 14/SouthLeith index details favour a separate person and do not establish the ploughman’s parentage.

The 1827trial comparison is superseded as a life-event attribution. The Crown Office precognition index AD14/27/25 and Edinburgh Lock-up House index HH21/8/1 p.11 both identify Alexander Glasgow, blacksmith, age 14 and born South Leith. The linked trial JC26/1827/326 names the same Alexander/John Paterson pair and housebreaking charge, with a 14-year transportation sentence. The age 14 and sentence 14 years are distinct indexed fields. The combined details strongly favour a younger circa 1812–1813-born accused, rather than the 1799Colinton child. Originals remain uninspected; this is a record-level identity correction, not a claim about the adult ploughman’s conduct. <ref name="Blacksmith1827">Scottish Indexes, [https://www.scottishindexes.com/adentry.aspx?adid=827025 AD14/27/25], [https://www.scottishindexes.com/jcdetail.aspx?jcid=1827326&pid=182732633 JC26/1827/326] and [https://www.scottishindexes.com/prisontranscript.aspx?prisonid=80101124 HH21/8/1 p.11], public index entries inspected30–31October2026. Original documents uninspected.</ref>

The proposed family amendment is to add [[Glasgow-1304|John Glasgow]] as the father of [[Glasgow-2695|Alexander Glasgow]], 65% probable. [[Glasgow-2718]] remains a separate possible childhood account. No live edit is claimed.
